newsitem.title: UK: UK farmers attack Hogg over beef crisis handling.
newsitem.headline: UK farmers attack Hogg over beef crisis handling.

text.p: British farmers said on Thursday they had no confidence in Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg to protect their interests in the beef crisis.

After a meeting on Thursday delegates to a Council meeting of the National Farmers Union (NFU) demanded a meeting with Prime Minister John Major to ensure its views were heard. "NFU Council has no confidence in the (Agriculture) Minister's representation of the interests of the UK and its agricultural industry in the European Union," its statement said. It was "immensely dismayed" that Hogg had lost touch with the concerns and needs of British agriculture.
The NFU Council called for a dramatic increase in culling to clear the backlog of cattle. The cull covers cattle more than 30 months old.
NFU also asked for a restoration of the recent cut in the compensation for cattle over 30 months old to one Ecu per kg from the current 0.9 Ecu.
Earlier this week, Hogg announced plans to speed up the cull and increase compensation for British farmers whose markets have been hit by the BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) scare.
The NFU said agreement was needed on short-term and long-term financial support for beef producers.
It declared October 26 as National Beef Day to encourage the promotion of beef.
